findings.title: No credential type/ownership scoping to calendar credentials only
findings.body: The handler validates the credential belongs to the user but doesn't restrict deletion to calendar-type credentials or verify it is actually a Google Calendar credential with cache data. Any credential ID owned by the user could trigger a (harmless but unintended) calendarCache.deleteMany call. More importantly, it does not check team/organization-owned credentials (e.g. via delegation) possibly leaving admins unable to delete cache for team-managed accounts, or conversely silently no-op without feedback since deleteMany on non-matching credentialId succeeds with 0 rows deleted, giving a false success response to the UI even if no cache existed.

findings.title: Unconditional updateManyByCredentialId call on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache
findings.body: After looping through all event-type groups, the code unconditionally calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to bump `updatedAt` for all calendars under the credential. This runs an extra UPDATE query on every call to fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache (used extensively in webhook/cron and cache refresh flows), with an empty `data` object relying on Prisma's `@updatedAt` auto-timestamp behavior. Doing this for every invocation adds additional DB load, and the empty `data: {}` pattern is fragile — if the `updatedAt` field were ever changed to not use `@updatedAt`, this call would silently do nothing useful while still issuing a query to all rows matching credentialId regardless of eventTypeId scoping, potentially touching more rows than intended within a single credential across multiple event types.

findings.title: updatedAt added with @updatedAt plus a migration-time default; comment is contradictory/misleading
findings.body: The field is declared `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt` with a comment saying "Provide an initial value for legacy rows and future raw inserts." However `@updatedAt` automatically manages the timestamp on every Prisma update, so the explicit `@default(now())` is only relevant for raw SQL inserts bypassing Prisma — but the migration itself already backfills existing rows with `DEFAULT NOW()`. This dual mechanism is redundant/confusing and could cause confusion for future maintainers about whether `updatedAt` reflects "row created" vs "cache value last updated", especially since cache entries are upserted via Prisma `upsert` (update branch) which already triggers `@updatedAt`.

findings.title: Hardcoded locale/date formatting ignores user locale and i18n
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is hardcoded, ignoring the app's `t`/i18n locale setting used elsewhere in the component. This causes an inconsistent experience for non-English users, showing dates in US format regardless of their chosen locale.

findings.title: Component return null leaves user without any affordance when disableConnectionModification and no cache
findings.body: When `canDisconnect` is false (delegation credential or disableConnectionModification) and there's no cache (`hasCache` false, e.g. non-Google calendar or Google with no cache yet), the component renders `null`. This silently removes any actions/ellipsis menu for that credential row with no visual indication, which is a behavior change versus the previous `DisconnectIntegration` component that likely rendered a disabled/absent state more predictably; combined with the PR replacing `DisconnectIntegration` entirely, non-Google calendar integrations (e.g., Outlook, Office365) lose any action affordance since `hasCache` is always false for them and disconnect may still be legitimately desired.

findings.title: Added fields to UserWithCalendars type not used/validated for all callers
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` fields to be selected, but this type is consumed by multiple callers constructing `UserWithCalendars` from various Prisma selects (e.g. withSelectedCalendars, platform libraries). If any caller doesn't select these new fields, this is a type-level breaking change that could cause runtime undefined errors or TypeScript failures outside the files shown in this diff that weren't updated to add the new select fields.
